html:
SMTO-LLM-0061 — Your model server profile has a setting SMTO can't use

GUID: 32035149-8fe0-5450-8b51-cbbe9b0dde3f
Slug: local-ai-profile-invalid
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: local_ai

What happened

  • Something in the model server profile doesn't fit the program or the chosen computer, a key it points to wasn't included, or the profile changed after this task started. SMTO stopped instead of guessing a fix.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Parameter Store, select the Local AI Runtime profile, and make sure host is a number address such as 127.0.0.1, not a name like localhost. SMTO only accepts number addresses for the model server's host.
  2. Check gateway_id matches the Node name shown for that Gateway in Settings › Setup › Gateways (ask the Gateway's manager if none is shown), and any working directory is a full folder path that exists there. A profile made for a different computer, or pointing to a missing folder, is refused.
  3. Remove extra options that don't belong to your program, keep any API key in a separate Local AI API key parameter, and select Save. Each program accepts its own options only, and keys must not sit inside the profile itself.
  4. Ask SMTO to show the Local AI status for that Gateway, then start the model server in a new message that names the profile, and its key if it has one, with @. The status shows whether an older version is still running; a new message uses the saved profile, and SMTO only uses a key you named.

What success looks like

  • SMTO accepts the profile and the model server reaches ready.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO or that Gateway. Don't paste an API key into the profile itself, and don't stop a running model server SMTO didn't start.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Local AI profile validation failed: an invalid field or provider option, a non-IP host, gateway_id not matching the Gateway's node name, a stale profile_revision, a bad executable or working_directory, an api_key_ref that is not an accepted Local AI API key Parameter, an unresolvable accepted profile binding, or a running runtime for the same profile at another revision.

What this means

  • Closed profile validation rejects unsupported values, stale revisions, wrong Gateway identity or incompatible executable/options. Local AI management belongs to the selected Gateway and accepted profile. Starting a runtime does not activate it for the controller; recorded execution and unknown-effect facts determine whether reconciliation is required.

Why this can happen

  • Closed profile validation rejects unsupported values, stale revisions, wrong Gateway identity or incompatible executable/options.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare Gateway identity, profile revision, executable, working directory and typed options with the rejected validation path.

How to fix it

  • Validate the Local AI Runtime Parameter against RuntimeProfile (gateway_core/local_ai/models.py): IP-literal host, provider-specific extra_options, an existing absolute working_directory, an executable basename matching the provider, gateway_id equal to the Gateway's node name, and api_key_ref pointing to a Local AI API key Parameter that is also an accepted reference of the task. Then start a new task using the current revision from local_ai.profiles; keep secrets in the separate key Parameter.
  • Correct the specific profile field and accept the updated revision; preserve secrets in their dedicated parameter references.

Retry and execution caution

  • Only after exact state reconciliation.

How to verify the fix

  • The exact accepted profile and arguments validate against the selected Gateway and provider.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations or stop externally owned processes.

Technical notes

  • Local AI management belongs to the selected Gateway and accepted profile. Starting a runtime does not activate it for the controller; recorded execution and unknown-effect facts determine whether reconciliation is required.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
